subject: Copywriting
title: Event-Triggered Emails
description: A micro-lesson that makes Event-Triggered Emails usable.

hook.text: Triggered emails—sent when a user acts—get 8x more opens than scheduled blasts. Timing is everything.

buildup.text: Events trigger emails: purchase, browse, download, birthday, inactivity.

discovery.text: Event-Triggered Emails reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Over-triggering creates fatigue. Buy a shirt, get five emails. Browse once, get stalked for a month. Restraint matters.

climax.text: The best triggered emails feel helpful, not surveillant. 'Your free trial ends tomorrow' helps.

punchline.text: Right message, right moment. Triggered emails are 8x more relevant.

quiz.question: How many more opens do triggered emails get compared to scheduled ones?

details.summary: Event-triggered emails are sent automatically when a user takes a specific action — viewing a product, hitting a milestone, or going inactive. Because they respond to actual behavior, triggered emails achieve 70.5% higher open rates and 152% higher click rates than batch campaigns.
details.whyItMatters: Triggered emails feel personal because they respond to what the subscriber just did. This relevance produces engagement rates that mass campaigns simply cannot match.
takeaways: Triggered emails respond to specific user actions in real time
They achieve 70% higher open rates than regular batch campaigns
Common triggers include purchases, page views, milestones, and inactivity

faq.question: What are the most valuable email triggers to implement?
faq.answer: Start with welcome (new signup), abandoned cart, post-purchase (review request), and inactivity (re-engagement). These four triggers cover the major lifecycle stages and produce the highest ROI. Add milestone and browse-abandonment triggers as your program matures.

faq.question: Why do triggered emails outperform regular campaigns?
faq.answer: Timing and relevance. A triggered email arrives exactly when the subscriber's interest is highest — right after they browsed a product, completed a purchase, or hit a milestone. This contextual relevance makes the email feel helpful rather than intrusive.
